data.title: Campbell’s Stock (CPB) Falls 10% After Soup Company Slashes Dividend 36%
data.description:
The stock of Campbell’s (CPB) is down 10% after the food company known for its soup cut its dividend by 36% in order to conserve cash. Campbell’s, which also makes consumer snacks, lowered its quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share from $0.39 previously. CPB previously had a dividend yield of 7.25%, one of the highest on Wall Street. Going forward, the yield will be 4.65%. The next dividend is payable on Nov. 2 to shareholders of record as of Oct. 1.

Management at Campbell’s said that the dividend was cut as part of a larger cost-cutting effort that’s aimed at safeguarding the company’s financial health amid weak consumer spending and a shift towards healthier eating habits. The company has also announced plans to close several plants and layoff workers as part of a cost-cutting drive that’s aimed at saving $500 million by 2030.

Campbell’s Financial Results

The dividend cut was announced along with Campbell’s latest financial results. The packaged food company reported earnings per share (EPS) of $0.39 a share for what was its fiscal fourth quarter, in line with Wall Street’s expectations. Quarterly revenue of $2.1 billion was also in line with analysts’ consensus forecasts. However, the company’s sales were down 8% year-over-year in the latest quarter.

The company guided for its net sales to fall between 2% and 4% this fiscal year. Analysts were expecting a decline of less than 1%.

data.title: 4 Fundamental Reasons Why I Believe Nike Stock (NKE) Hasn’t Bottomed Yet
data.description:
Nike (NKE) has flirted with a bottom a few times this year, but so far, none of those attempts have looked definitive. The Beaverton, Oregon-based sportswear giant entered its latest earnings report already down about 39% in 2026. Since then, it has slipped back toward its 12-month lows.

The latest quarter did bring some relief. Nike reported earnings per share (EPS) of $0.72 versus $0.12 expected, while revenue of $10.97 billion also beat consensus in Q4 FY2026. Matthew Friend, Executive Vice President and CFO, said, “We delivered fourth quarter results in line with our expectations, demonstrating financial discipline in an increasingly challenging operating environment, where sell-through remains challenged.”

However, sales still fell about 1% year-over-year. More importantly, Nike still faces weak forward guidance, uncertain market-share trends, a valuation that does not yet fully reflect the risks, and a dividend that needs healthier free cash flow (FCF) to remain comfortable.

data.title: Alibaba Stock (BABA) Sell-Off May Have Further to Run
data.description:
Alibaba (BABA) stock sell-off may have further to run. The ADR fell sharply last Friday, with losses extended further Monday morning after the company unveiled a $10.2 billion equity placement. Fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 9% to $39.64 billion, yet adjusted EBITA fell 30%.

Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) per ADR also dropped 42%, and net income collapsed 75%. Yes, its 45% cloud growth sounds impressive. However, nearly $10 billion of quarterly capital expenditure pushed free cash flow to a $6.58 billion outflow. With commerce slowing and artificial intelligence (AI) economics still unproven, I remain bearish despite the lower share price. This is especially true since current holders must absorb any ongoing dilution.

For context, Alibaba is a Chinese multinational conglomerate operating across e-commerce, cloud computing, digital media, and fintech, though it remains best known for its flagship e-commerce platforms.
